mixed4b:237.bare_s1: The unit responds to the side windows of motor vehicles, especially the cab or front door window of cars, trucks, vans and similar vehicles.
mixed4b:237.bare_s2: The unit responds to the side windows of road vehicles (the cab or door window glass with its frame) on cars, trucks, vans and RVs.
mixed4b:237.Q0_s1: The unit responds to the side window of a vehicle cab, i.e. the glass area of a car, truck, van or bus door/window, seen in side or three-quarter view.
mixed4b:237.Q0_s2: The unit responds to the side windows of road vehicles, especially the driver/cab door window area of cars, trucks, vans and buses.
mixed4b:237.F1_s1: The unit responds to a roughly rectangular, glossy, dark or see-through region with rounded corners, outlined by a thin frame and set into a smooth, evenly colored, curved painted surface, often split by a narrow vertical bar and with a small protrusion at its lower front corner.
mixed4b:237.F1_s2: The unit responds to a dark or reflective, roughly trapezoidal glossy pane outlined by a thin frame, often split by a narrow vertical bar, set into a smooth, uniformly colored painted surface.
mixed4b:237.wrong: The unit responds broadly to man-made, often handcrafted or decorated objects such as fabric items, ornaments, accessories and gear. It may be keyed to curved, bordered or seamed contours, or to ornamental patterns on those objects, but no single concept is clear.

mixed4b:491.bare_s1: The unit responds to the lower side body of road vehicles (cars, vans, trucks, buses, RVs), especially around the wheel wells and front wheel/fender area. It also responds weakly to related vehicle parts such as a car dashboard stereo.
mixed4b:491.bare_s2: The unit responds to the side and lower body of road vehicles (cars, vans, trucks, buses, RVs), especially the region around the front wheel and wheel arch.
mixed4b:491.Q0_s1: The unit responds to the lower side body of road vehicles, especially the wheel and wheel-arch region of cars, vans, trucks, buses and RVs. A weaker, related extension covers car interior parts such as a dashboard radio.
mixed4b:491.Q0_s2: The unit responds to the lower side bodywork of road vehicles (cars, vans, trucks, buses, RVs), especially around the front wheel arch and fender. A weaker extension covers other car parts, such as an in-dash car radio.
mixed4b:491.F1_s1: The unit responds to a smooth, glossy, uniformly colored painted surface broken by a curved arched cutout that frames a dark, round, spoked or ribbed disc, often with nearby horizontal trim lines or small rectangular bright inserts. Weaker responses come from the same smooth, rounded panel edges and seams without the dark disc.
mixed4b:491.F1_s2: The unit responds to smooth, glossy, uniformly colored panel surfaces whose lower edge curves into an arched cutout that frames a dark, ring-like round shape with a lighter radial center. It is most active where the painted surface's curved seam or edge meets that dark circular form.
mixed4b:491.wrong: The unit responds to the faces of dogs, especially the eye/upper-cheek area. It also responds somewhat less to closely related canids such as wolves and foxes.

mixed4b:373.bare_s1: The unit detects the front wheel of a road vehicle seen from the side or at an angle: the tire, rim and the wheel-arch region of cars, vans, buses, trucks and fire engines.
mixed4b:373.bare_s2: The unit detects the wheels of road vehicles, specifically the wheel and tire seen from the side, often including the wheel arch, on cars, vans, buses, trucks and emergency vehicles.
mixed4b:373.Q0_s1: The unit detects the wheels of road vehicles, most likely the front wheel and wheel-arch region, across cars, trucks, buses, fire engines and emergency vehicles.
mixed4b:373.Q0_s2: The unit responds to the wheels of road vehicles (cars, vans, trucks, buses, fire engines), specifically the front wheel and the wheel-arch region around it.
mixed4b:373.F1_s1: The unit responds to a dark, round, ring-shaped form with a lighter center that has radial spokes, sitting inside an arched cutout along the lower edge of a large, smooth, often brightly colored panel.
mixed4b:373.F1_s2: The unit responds to a dark, thick circular ring around a lighter, spoked or radially patterned center, sitting inside a curved arch cut into a smooth, brightly colored, glossy surface, usually near the lower edge of a large boxy shape.
mixed4b:373.wrong: The unit mainly responds to road vehicles (cars, vans, trucks, buses), firing on the side body panel near the front door or wheel. It also responds, separately, to dogs.

mixed4b:443.bare_s1: The unit responds to the faces of dogs, especially the eye/upper-cheek area. It also responds somewhat less to closely related canids such as wolves and foxes.
mixed4b:443.bare_s2: The unit detects the eye/upper-face region of dog faces, and responds somewhat less strongly to the same region on dog-like canids such as wolves and foxes.
mixed4b:443.Q0_s1: The unit responds to dog faces, especially the eye and upper-face region. It also responds, slightly more weakly, to the faces of closely related canids such as wolves and foxes.
mixed4b:443.Q0_s2: The unit responds to the faces of dogs and other canids, peaking on the eye and upper-muzzle region.
mixed4b:443.F1_s1: The unit responds most to the furred patch beside and just above the eye on a frontal, long-snouted head, where fur texture meets the eye and cheek contour below the ear. It responds less to similar fur-and-eye textures on heads with a different overall shape.
mixed4b:443.F1_s2: The unit responds to the patch of short, directional fur just beside and around an eye on a front-facing face with a protruding snout, where the eye's dark rim meets the surrounding hair and the muzzle begins.
mixed4b:443.wrong: The unit responds to the side windows of motor vehicles, especially the cab or front door window of cars, trucks, vans and similar vehicles.

mixed4b:431.bare_s1: The unit responds to furry mammal fur/coat texture, most strongly on dogs and dog-like canids (dhole, hyena), especially on the head, ears, and neck/shoulder region. It extends more weakly to other furry mammals such as monkeys, hamsters, squirrels, and minks.
mixed4b:431.bare_s2: Responds to the fur of mammals, mainly dogs and dog-like canids, where the box usually sits on furry head, ear, or body regions. Weaker responses come from other furry mammals such as monkeys, a hyena, a hamster, a squirrel, and a mink.
mixed4b:431.Q0_s1: The unit mainly responds to dogs, especially furry regions such as ears, cheeks and coat, and responds somewhat less to other furry mammals.
mixed4b:431.Q0_s2: The unit responds to furry mammal fur/coat texture, especially on dogs (ears, cheeks, chest), with weaker extension to other furry mammals such as monkeys, hyena, hamster, squirrel and mink.
mixed4b:431.F1_s1: The unit responds to soft, dense, fine-strand texture: short, directional, fluffy grain covering rounded body surfaces. It is strongest on warm brown, tan or grey tufted patches near the edges of rounded forms.
mixed4b:431.F1_s2: The unit responds to dense, soft, fine-stranded fibrous texture with fuzzy, low-contrast edges, mostly in warm brown, tan, gray or black tones. It fires most on smooth, flowing regions of this texture next to a subject's head or upper body.
mixed4b:431.wrong: The unit detects the front wheel of a road vehicle seen from the side or at an angle: the tire, rim and the wheel-arch region of cars, vans, buses, trucks and fire engines.

mixed4c:254.bare_s1: The unit mainly responds to thin, upright vertical structures such as screw shafts, tail fins, masts, antennas, handles and slots, mostly on man-made objects. It responds more weakly to vertical frame edges like car and tractor cab window pillars.
mixed4c:254.bare_s2: The unit seems to respond to thin, upright structures that stick up from an object, such as posts, pillars, fins, masts, antennas and window frames, most strongly on man-made objects and vehicles. Weaker hits on animal necks and heads look like the same vertical-upright shape on natural things.
mixed4c:254.Q0_s1: The unit responds mainly to thin vertical upright structures on man-made objects, such as poles, masts, tail fins, screw shanks, antennas, handles, and the vertical pillars and frames of vehicle cab windows. It responds more weakly to vertical shapes on animals, such as an ostrich neck or a fox's upright head.
mixed4c:254.Q0_s2: The unit mainly responds to thin vertical upright structures such as poles, shafts, masts, tail fins, antennas and window pillars, mostly on man-made objects. It also responds more weakly to related framed rectangular openings like vehicle cab windows and toaster slots.
mixed4c:254.F1_s1: The unit responds mainly to narrow, upright, straight-edged bars or slender vertical protrusions, especially where they meet a contrasting background. It responds more weakly to small vertically oriented rectangular openings or frames bounded by such straight vertical edges.
mixed4c:254.F1_s2: The unit responds to narrow, upright, elongated vertical strips or bars, often thin parallel vertical edges or slightly tapered verticals that contrast with their surroundings.
mixed4c:254.wrong: The unit responds to the lower side body of road vehicles (cars, vans, trucks, buses, RVs), especially around the wheel wells and front wheel/fender area. It also responds weakly to related vehicle parts such as a car dashboard stereo.

mixed4c:407.bare_s1: The unit responds mainly to the chin, throat and upper-chest area just below a dog's face (often including an open mouth or tongue). It responds somewhat more weakly to the same region on similar animals such as wolves, a ferret, a monkey and even a bird.
mixed4c:407.bare_s2: The unit responds to the throat, chin and upper chest just below the muzzle of dogs and wolves, often including an open mouth or tongue. It responds more weakly to the same neck region on other furry animals and birds.
mixed4c:407.Q0_s1: The unit responds to the throat/chest/lower-muzzle region of animals, mostly dogs and wolves, and also fires on other furry or feathered animals' necks.
mixed4c:407.Q0_s2: The unit responds to the throat, chest and lower-muzzle area of dogs and wolves, including open mouths with tongues. It also fires, nearly as strongly, on the same neck and chest region of other animals such as a bird, a ferret and a monkey.
mixed4c:407.F1_s1: The unit responds to the area just below a forward-facing head where a soft, finely fibrous surface curves into a broader body mass, often with a lighter patch or a small pink protruding shape beneath the jaw line. The response is strongest when the region is lit, mid-frame and fills a moderate part of the image.
mixed4c:407.F1_s2: The unit responds to the narrow region just below a forward-pointing head shape, where a face meets a neck or chest, especially when the surface there has fine, soft, hair-like texture. It responds more weakly to a glossy pink lobe hanging from an open mouth-like opening and to finely streaked versions of the same neck-region texture.
mixed4c:407.wrong: The unit responds broadly to man-made, often handcrafted or decorated objects such as fabric items, ornaments, accessories and gear. It may be keyed to curved, bordered or seamed contours, or to ornamental patterns on those objects, but no single concept is clear.

mixed5a:719.bare_s1: The unit responds broadly to man-made, often handcrafted or decorated objects such as fabric items, ornaments, accessories and gear. It may be keyed to curved, bordered or seamed contours, or to ornamental patterns on those objects, but no single concept is clear.
mixed5a:719.bare_s2: The unit appears to respond to the surfaces of close-up, product-style photos of man-made objects, most strongly crafted or decorated items such as textiles, ornaments, embossed or patterned surfaces, and accessories. Plainer manufactured objects like the mouse, knee pads and shoes look like weaker extensions of the same theme.
mixed5a:719.Q0_s1: The unit seems to mix at least two unconnected features: ornamental, often floral or stitched decorative patterns on crafted objects (crochet, brooch, manhole cover, teapot carving, bib, basket, Christmas stocking) and smooth, glossy dark molded surfaces (computer mouse, knee pads, toy gun, armor). Its common ground is only broad: close-up photos of man-made objects.
mixed5a:719.Q0_s2: The unit seems to respond to close-up views of handcrafted or decorated man-made objects, especially fabric and sewn items such as stockings, cushions, bibs, bow ties and crochet. It extends more weakly to other ornamented or smooth-edged objects like armor, a teapot, a manhole cover and a computer mouse.
mixed5a:719.F1_s1: The unit responds to smooth, rounded, arc-shaped contours where a curved surface meets its border, especially when that border is outlined, trimmed or stitched. It responds more weakly to ornamental radial motifs made of repeated lobed shapes spreading from a center.
mixed5a:719.F1_s2: The unit responds mainly to smooth, uniformly colored crafted surfaces bounded by crisp curved outlines or seams. It responds more weakly to flat, stylized decorative motifs such as radial petal-like shapes, stars and printed patterns on those surfaces.
mixed5a:719.wrong: The unit mainly responds to thin, upright vertical structures such as screw shafts, tail fins, masts, antennas, handles and slots, mostly on man-made objects. It responds more weakly to vertical frame edges like car and tractor cab window pillars.

mixed4d:417.bare_s1: The unit mainly responds to road vehicles (cars, vans, trucks, buses), firing on the side body panel near the front door or wheel. It also responds, separately, to dogs.
mixed4d:417.bare_s2: The unit responds mainly to road vehicles (cars, vans, trucks, buses), peaking on the body panel near the front wheel or door. It also responds to dogs, a second concept with no meaningful link to vehicles.
mixed4d:417.Q0_s1: The unit responds mainly to road vehicles (cars, vans, pickups, buses, emergency vehicles), peaking on the body panel or wheel-arch region. It also responds separately to dogs.
mixed4d:417.Q0_s2: The unit responds mainly to road vehicles (cars, trucks, buses, vans), peaking on the side or front body panel near the wheel arch or door. It also responds separately to dogs.
mixed4d:417.F1_s1: The unit responds most strongly to a mid-sized region of smooth, evenly colored, gently curved surface bounded by a crisp contour, with a large dark rounded shape just below and a horizontal edge or seam running across it. It responds more weakly to broad, uniformly toned furry or textured flanks with a similar shape and scale.
mixed4d:417.F1_s2: The unit responds to the broad side flank of a large, bulky, side-on body: a fairly uniform surface patch at mid-height, just above and behind a rounded lower contour, often with a crease or seam crossing it. It responds most to smooth, glossy, single-colored versions of this surface and more weakly to soft, textured versions.
mixed4d:417.wrong: The unit responds to furry mammal fur/coat texture, most strongly on dogs and dog-like canids (dhole, hyena), especially on the head, ears, and neck/shoulder region. It extends more weakly to other furry mammals such as monkeys, hamsters, squirrels, and minks.

mixed4d:241.bare_s1: The unit responds to two unconnected things: the faces of shaggy, long-haired dogs (terrier and sheepdog types), and the side bodywork of road vehicles such as cars, vans and pickup trucks, usually near the doors or wheel wells.
mixed4d:241.bare_s2: The unit responds to two unrelated things: the faces and heads of shaggy, long-haired dogs (terriers, Bouviers, Tibetan-type breeds), and the side body panels and doors of cars, vans, and pickup trucks.
mixed4d:241.Q0_s1: The unit responds to two separate things: the faces of shaggy, long-haired dogs (terriers, Bouviers, Yorkies) and the side body panels of cars, vans and pickup trucks, usually near the front door or wheel well.
mixed4d:241.Q0_s2: The unit responds to two unrelated things: the faces of shaggy, long-haired dogs (terriers, Bouviers, Yorkies, schnauzer-like breeds) and the side body panels and doors of cars, trucks and vans.
mixed4d:241.F1_s1: The unit responds to a mid-scale, compact rounded region where darker blobs or curved contour lines sit inside a curved outer boundary, set against a contrasting, more uniform surround. It looks like a detector for 'enclosed dark rounded features framed by an arc' rather than for any particular texture or colour.
mixed4d:241.F1_s2: Under the assumption of one shared pattern, the unit responds best to a compact, mid-sized patch where a broad surface of fairly uniform tone or texture is broken by darker rounded features, such as a curved dark hollow or a cluster of dark spots. Those features are framed by gently curving edges or seams.
mixed4d:241.wrong: The unit responds mainly to the chin, throat and upper-chest area just below a dog's face (often including an open mouth or tongue). It responds somewhat more weakly to the same region on similar animals such as wolves, a ferret, a monkey and even a bird.

mixed4d:277.bare_s1: The unit responds to at least two unconnected things: the heads or bodies of animals (fox, coyote, gazelle, ibex, rabbits, spiders) and the side panels or doors of road vehicles, especially fire trucks, taxis, ambulances and buses.
mixed4d:277.bare_s2: The unit is polysemantic and responds to at least three unconnected things: the heads of small to medium mammals (fox, gazelle, rabbit, ibex, coyote), spider bodies, and the side and door areas of commercial or emergency vehicles (taxis, fire trucks, ambulances, a bus).
mixed4d:277.Q0_s1: The unit appears to respond to two unconnected things: the heads or bodies of wild animals (fox, coyote, rabbit, gazelle and ibex heads, and spider bodies), and the side panels or doors of service vehicles (fire trucks, taxis, an ambulance, a snow truck and a minibus).
mixed4d:277.Q0_s2: The unit appears polysemantic, responding to two unconnected things: wild animals, mostly the heads of small or medium mammals (fox, gazelle, rabbit, ibex, coyote) plus spider bodies, and large service or commercial vehicles (fire trucks, taxis, ambulance, utility trucks, bus), usually on the door or side-panel area.
mixed4d:277.F1_s1: The unit responds to a compact, roughly symmetric patch of fine, high-contrast detail sitting at the center of a larger, smoother region of fairly uniform color or texture, especially when thin elongated shapes radiate or stick out from that patch. Weaker responses come from small detailed marks or insignia placed on large flat colored panels.
mixed4d:277.F1_s2: The unit responds to a compact, roughly centered focal region bounded by strong contours, with thin elongated projections or sharp edges branching outward from it, often in symmetric pairs.
mixed4d:277.wrong: The unit responds to the faces of dogs, especially the eye/upper-cheek area. It also responds somewhat less to closely related canids such as wolves and foxes.
